title: Air Cycle Machine Turbine Silencer and Bearing Assembly Change for Rear Cabin Sound Pressure Reduction

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: A revised turbine silencer and an oil-damped bearing cartridge in the air cycle machine remove a tonal component at 3.2 kilohertz that dominates the measured sound pressure level in the rearmost seat rows.

sections.reason: Cabin comfort surveys carried out for three launch customers of the higher-density layout identified a persistent tonal component at 3.2 kilohertz in the last six seat rows, measured at 8 dB above the broadband level and traced to the second-stage turbine of the air cycle machine. The tone appears only above 88 per cent machine speed, which is the normal cruise condition on a full cabin. It is not a defect and drives no maintenance action, but it was the single largest contributor to the comfort score in the rear cabin and three operators made it a condition of their next order.
sections.description: The turbine outlet silencer is replaced by an accumulator-style item KEDE723823-59 with a longer expansion volume and a perforated liner tuned to the offending harmonic, and the machine hose LU579123-82 is re-routed with a longer radius to move its first structural mode away from the same frequency. The restrictor D2150113216257 in the bypass leg is changed to hold the machine below the tonal speed band during cruise, and the washer EN911564K9 under the mount foot is replaced by a bonded elastomeric item that decouples the casing from the pack bay structure. The machine filter FIN 312HM and the non-return valve FIN 33HQ are unchanged; the pipe FIN 4HM is re-clipped. Work is done in the pack bay, zones 191 and 192, with the belly fairing panels removed. Drawings D21500081959 issue B and D21501246663 issue F carry the silencer and mount detail.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 6.3 kg per pack, two packs per aircraft, essentially on the centre line with no balance effect. No electrical load change. The silencer is one-way interchangeable: the new item fits the old machine but the old item does not achieve the acoustic result on the new mount. Pack performance is unchanged at the certified flow; the bypass restrictor costs about 0.4 per cent in maximum cooling capacity at hot-day ground conditions, which remains inside the certified envelope. Measured sound pressure level in seat rows 24 to 30 falls by 4.1 dB(A). AMM removal and installation content for ATA 21-50 was re-issued.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN Z09899 in May 2018. Retrofit is a two-shift task per pack with the belly fairing open and is normally combined with a pack overhaul, so most operators embody it on condition rather than as a campaign.

type_data.balance_impact: Centre line installation, no measurable CG effect
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN Z09899, absorbed in the pack installation station
